newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico govt to auction 160,000 home credits in '97.
newsitem.headline: Mexico govt to auction 160,000 home credits in '97.

text.p: The Mexican government's subsidised housing agency Fovi plans to auction rights to grant 160,000 mortgages in 1997, agency director Manuel Cepeda said on Monday.

"Subject to approval by the Fovi board, I believe that...we will auction mortgages for 160,000 homes for the year," Cepeda said at a meeting of the local branch of the Real Estate and Housing Developers' Association (Adivac).
"There is a Fovi board meeting on Tuesday, which will approve the schedule of mortgage auctions...we will have eight auctions, one every 45 days for 20,000 homes on each fixed date," he said.

Cepeda said that Fovi would begin an additional programme to help people earning up to two-and-a-half times the minimum wage to acquire homes of their own. The minimum wage in Mexico City is 22.60 pesos ($2.87) a day.
The programme would grant housing developers access to an "enormous market" of people who are not currently considered creditworthy for housing schemes, he said.
In addition to the special programme, Cepeda said a programme to subsidise savings to bolster the plan would be introduced.
"There will be a programme with a 20 percent up-front subsidy, in cash, government funds for 20 percent of the value of the home, plus a minimum down payment of 10 percent," Cepeda said.
Fovi's normal programme would also have a subsidised savings scheme, he said.
"Reforms to income tax law are being looked into to favour savings," he said.
Cepeda also said that Fovi was planning an "issue of mortgage-backed bonds" to channel more funds into the housing sector.
